points: Basic repro: `@SuperBuilder class ChildWithAnnotation extends Parent<@ValidDouble Double>` with generic `Parent<T extends Comparable<T>>` → generated `ChildWithAnnotationBuilder<C,B> extends Parent.ParentBuilder<...>` has 3 type args (Double, C, B), compiles, and delombok output matches the non-annotated Child case (before/after-delombok/after-ecj triple)

Multiple type arguments where only some are annotated, e.g. `Parent2<@A String, Integer, @B Long>` → all superclass type args are preserved in order and followed by C, B (count = superclass type params + 2)

Annotation with parameters, e.g. `extends Parent<@TA(x=5) Double>` → type arg is kept (annotation retained or cleanly stripped consistently) and the code compiles with a build() that returns the child type

Nested generic with annotation inside, e.g. `extends Parent<List<@A String>>` and a fully-qualified annotated type `Parent<java.lang.@A Double>` → type args are not dropped and the builder extends clause is valid

Non-annotated superclass type args (`Child extends Parent<Double>`) and existing SuperBuilderWithGenerics cases still generate identical output (no regression); the builder can be used: `ChildWithAnnotation.builder().value(1.0).build()`
Other non-handled type-arg kinds (wildcard `Parent<? extends Number>` or array type args) → not silently dropped; the superclass builder gets the correct number of type arguments
